title: Gamelan: the bronze orchestra of Indonesia
examples: What instruments are in a gamelan?
What is the big gong for?

groups.label: Gongs
groups.ask: What is the big gong for?

explain.say: Imagine an orchestra where almost every instrument is made of shining bronze, glowing gold, and all the players sit on the floor together. That is a gamelan, from the islands of Java and Bali in Indonesia. Look at the board: let us sort its instruments.

draw.text: Gamelan: the bronze orchestra of Indonesia

groups.label: Gongs
groups.ask: What is the big gong for?

explain.say: Look at the gongs. The biggest, the gong ageng, can be about a metre wide. Smaller kettle gongs, like the kenong and bonang, sit in wooden frames. When you strike a gong, its sound shimmers for a long time. Have you ever heard a gong ring?

groups.label: Gongs
groups.ask: What is the big gong for?

explain.say: Now the metal keys. A saron is a row of bronze bars you hit with a hammer, a bit like a xylophone. Then look at the last group: the kendang drum, a bamboo flute called suling, a fiddle called rebab, and singers. Which one would you most like to play?

groups.label: Gongs
groups.ask: What is the big gong for?

explain.say: Gamelan music goes round in cycles, like a clock. Look at the circle: the saron plays the melody, the kenong and kempul mark the phrases, the kendang drummer steers, and the big gong closes the cycle. Then it all begins again! Where does each cycle end?

stages.note: Metal keys play the main tune, beat by beat

stages.label: Kenong marks
stages.note: A pot gong marks each phrase

stages.label: Kempul answers
stages.note: A hanging gong fills in between

stages.label: Kendang steers
stages.note: The drummer leads the speed and changes

stages.label: Big gong: the end
stages.note: Gong ageng closes the cycle; it starts again
stages.ask: What is the big gong for?

explain.say: Yes, on the big gong! Wonderful listening. A gamelan is played as a team, with no single star, and players take care not to step over the instruments. Wow fact: the French composer Debussy heard a Javanese gamelan in Paris in 1889, and it changed his music. Challenge: tap a 4 beat cycle and say gong on the last beat.

faq.a: A gamelan is a traditional ensemble from Indonesia, especially Java and Bali, made up mostly of bronze gongs and metal-keyed instruments, with drums, flute, fiddle and voices. The players perform together as a team.

faq.q: What is the big gong for?
faq.a: The gong ageng, the biggest gong, marks the end of each musical cycle. Its deep, long sound is the most important moment in the cycle, after which the pattern begins again.
asks: Why is the big gong important?

faq.a: A saron is a gamelan instrument with thick bronze bars on a wooden frame, struck with a mallet. Sarons usually play the main melody.
asks: What plays the melody in gamelan?
Is a saron like a xylophone?

faq.a: There is no conductor. The kendang drummer usually leads, signalling changes of speed and when to start and stop, and everyone listens closely to each other.
asks: Does a gamelan have a conductor?

faq.a: They are the two tuning systems of Javanese gamelan. Slendro has five notes to an octave, spaced fairly evenly; pelog has seven unevenly spaced notes. Each gamelan is tuned to itself, so instruments are not swapped between sets.

facts: Javanese gamelan uses two tuning systems: slendro with five notes and pelog with seven.
Claude Debussy heard a Javanese gamelan at the Paris Exposition Universelle of 1889.
UNESCO added gamelan to its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2021.

quiz.say: In a gamelan, which instrument marks the end of each cycle?
quiz.show: Each gamelan cycle ends on the…
quiz.why: The big gong ageng closes every cycle.

wrong.1: The suling is a bamboo flute that decorates the melody.
wrong.2: The rebab is a fiddle that leads some melodies.

quiz.say: Most gamelan instruments are made of what?
quiz.show: Most gamelan instruments are made of…
quiz.why: Gamelan gongs and metal keys are traditionally made of bronze.

wrong.1: Glass would break when struck with mallets.
wrong.2: Traditional gamelan uses metal, not plastic.
